ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, a bowl-shaped structure composed of folded polygonal faces can be seen; inside there are gray dashed lines, indicating the obscured central square base face and the overlapping edges between adjacent hexagons; the thick solid lines on the periphery connect into a circle of eight vertices of the bowl mouth, namely the rim octagon required by the problem. Reasoning: According to the specified three-dimensional coordinate model, put the central square with side length 1 in the z=0 plane, and take the vertices as (±1/2, ±1/2, 0). Let the unit direction of the north-side hexagon in its face, perpendicular to the common square edge and outward, be p_N. In a regular hexagon, the edge vector from a square corner point to an adjacent free vertex is 1/2 along the square-edge direction plus (√3/2)p_N. Adjacent hexagons share this edge at a square corner; by four-fold symmetry, one may let p_N=(0,a,b), p_E=(a,0,b), p_S=(0,-a,b), p_W=(-a,0,b). Comparing the shared edge of the north-side and west-side hexagons at the northwest corner gives a=1/√3; also p_N is a unit vector, so b=sqrt(1-1/3)=sqrt(2/3). Therefore p_N=(0,1/√3,sqrt(2/3)), and the other directions are similar. The two bowl-mouth vertices of the north-side hexagon are the two endpoints of the north edge plus √3 p_N, namely (-1/2,3/2,√2) and (1/2,3/2,√2). Similarly, all eight bowl-mouth vertices are on the same horizontal plane z=√2, and their xy projections in order are (-1/2,3/2), (1/2,3/2), (3/2,1/2), (3/2,-1/2), (1/2,-3/2), (-1/2,-3/2), (-3/2,-1/2), (-3/2,1/2). Therefore the required area is equal to the projected area of this planar octagon. This octagon can be regarded as a square with side length 3 with four right triangles whose right-angle sides are both 1 removed, and its area is 3×3 - 4×(1/2×1×1)=9-2=7.

method.method_draft: Use a full 3D coordinate model. From the image, take the hidden/dashed square as the central base and the solid outer boundary as the rim octagon; the dashed slanted lines show that neighboring hexagons share one edge at each square corner. Put the square of side 1 in the plane z=0 with vertices (±1/2,±1/2,0). For the hexagon attached to the north side, let its in-face outward unit direction be p_N. In a regular hexagon, the edge from a square corner to the adjacent free vertex has vector (1/2 along the square side)+(√3/2)p_N. Equate this same shared edge with the corresponding edge of the perpendicular neighboring hexagon; symmetry gives p_N=(0,1/√3,√(2/3)) and analogues for the other three sides. The two top vertices of the north hexagon are therefore the square-side endpoints plus √3 p_N: (-1/2,3/2,√2) and (1/2,3/2,√2), and similarly for the other sides. The eight rim vertices all have z=√2 and project to (-1/2,3/2),(1/2,3/2),(3/2,1/2),(3/2,-1/2),(1/2,-3/2),(-1/2,-3/2),(-3/2,-1/2),(-3/2,1/2). Compute the area of this octagon by shoelace or as a 3 by 3 square with four right triangles of legs 1 removed, giving 9-4(1/2)=7.

method.method_draft: Use a projection-and-dissection argument rather than solving for every coordinate. From the image, identify the rim as four unit top edges of the hexagons plus four connecting segments across the corners; the dashed seams show where adjacent hexagons share the same slanted edge from each square corner. By fourfold symmetry, the eight top vertices lie in a plane parallel to the square, so the rim area can be computed from its projection onto the square’s plane. At one square corner, the shared seam is simultaneously an edge of two regular hexagons attached to perpendicular sides. In a regular hexagon, the edge adjacent to the attached side has a tangential component 1/2 and an outward component √3/2 in the face; matching the perpendicular neighbor forces the seam’s horizontal projection to have equal components 1/2 and 1/2 along the two square directions. Continuing one more regular-hexagon edge to the actual top rim vertex cancels the tangential half-step and adds another outward half-step, so each top edge of a hexagon projects to a unit segment parallel to its square side and exactly 1 unit outside that side. Thus the projected rim octagon is obtained from the unit square by shifting each side outward by 1 and joining adjacent shifted endpoints: equivalently, it is a 3 by 3 square with four 1-by-1 corner right triangles cut off. Its area is 9-4·1/2=7.

图像描述：两幅附图都显示同一个碗状多面体：中间有一个边长为 1 的方形底面，四周各连着一个边长为 1 的正六边形面。黑色实线画出外侧可见边，灰色虚线表示被遮挡或相邻六边形共用的接缝。碗口由四个六边形的上方顶点连成，形成一个八边形的 rim。图中也可看出相邻六边形在方形角附近沿同一条斜边重合。
推理：用投影与分割的方法。由于四个正六边形围绕正方形按四重对称方式连接，碗口的八个顶点在一个与底部正方形平行的平面内，所以这个八边形的面积等于它正交投影到底面所在平面后的面积。
看底部正方形的一个角。图中的虚线接缝表示相邻两个六边形共用同一条从方形角出发的斜边。对边长为 1 的正六边形来说，与所附着的方形边相邻的一条边，在六边形面内可分解为沿方形边方向的 1/2 分量和向外方向的 √3/2 分量。因为这个接缝同时属于沿两条互相垂直方形边附着的两个六边形，匹配后它在水平投影中的两个方向分量相等，都是 1/2。
继续沿正六边形再走一条边到真正的碗口顶点时，沿原方形边方向的半步被抵消，而向外方向再增加半步。因此，每个六边形的上边投影为一条长为 1、与对应方形边平行、且距离该方形边正好为 1 的线段。
所以投影后的碗口八边形可以看作：从边长 1 的正方形出发，把四条边都向外平移 1，再连接相邻端点。若原正方形为 [0,1]×[0,1]，则八边形顶点可写为 (0,-1),(1,-1),(2,0),(2,1),(1,2),(0,2),(-1,1),(-1,0)。它等价于一个 3×3 正方形去掉四个直角边长均为 1 的角三角形。因此面积为 9−4·(1/2)=7。

所以投影后的碗口八边形可以看作：从边长 1 的正方形出发，把四条边都向外平移 1，再连接相邻端点。若原正方形为 [0,1]×[0,1]，则八边形顶点可写为 (0,-1),(1,-1),(2,0),(2,1),(1,2),(0,2),(-1,1),(-1,0)。它等价于一个 3×3 正方形去掉四个直角边长均为 1 的角三角形。因此面积为 9−4·(1/2)=7。

raw_record.original_question: A bowl is formed by attaching four regular hexagons of side 1 to a square of side 1. The edges of adjacent hexagons coincide, as shown in the figure. What is the area of the octagon obtained by joining the top eight vertices of the four hexagons, situated on the rim of the bowl?
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the attached figure, a bowl-shaped structure composed of folded polygonal faces can be seen; inside there are gray dashed lines, indicating the obscured central square base face and the overlapping edges between adjacent hexagons; the thick solid lines on the periphery connect into a circle of eight vertices of the bowl mouth, namely the rim octagon required by the problem.
Reasoning: According to the specified three-dimensional coordinate model, put the central square with side length 1 in the z=0 plane, and take the vertices as (±1/2, ±1/2, 0). Let the unit direction of the north-side hexagon in its face, perpendicular to the common square edge and outward, be p_N. In a regular hexagon, the edge vector from a square corner point to an adjacent free vertex is 1/2 along the square-edge direction plus (√3/2)p_N. Adjacent hexagons share this edge at a square corner; by four-fold symmetry, one may let p_N=(0,a,b), p_E=(a,0,b), p_S=(0,-a,b), p_W=(-a,0,b). Comparing the shared edge of the north-side and west-side hexagons at the northwest corner gives a=1/√3; also p_N is a unit vector, so b=sqrt(1-1/3)=sqrt(2/3). Therefore p_N=(0,1/√3,sqrt(2/3)), and the other directions are similar. The two bowl-mouth vertices of the north-side hexagon are the two endpoints of the north edge plus √3 p_N, namely (-1/2,3/2,√2) and (1/2,3/2,√2). Similarly, all eight bowl-mouth vertices are on the same horizontal plane z=√2, and their xy projections in order are (-1/2,3/2), (1/2,3/2), (3/2,1/2), (3/2,-1/2), (1/2,-3/2), (-1/2,-3/2), (-3/2,-1/2), (-3/2,1/2). Therefore the required area is equal to the projected area of this planar octagon. This octagon can be regarded as a square with side length 3 with four right triangles whose right-angle sides are both 1 removed, and its area is 3×3 - 4×(1/2×1×1)=9-2=7.
